newsitem.title: UK: Strong US Q2 oil demand offsets weaker Europe -IEA.
newsitem.headline: Strong US Q2 oil demand offsets weaker Europe -IEA.

text.p: Much stronger than expected oil demand in the U.S. in June offset weaker European consumption to lift OECD demand in the second quarter, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Tuesday.

The IEA pointed to "very robust demand growth in the U.S." when revising up its estimate of second quarter OECD growth by 215,000 barrels per day (bpd), or 2.6 percent, to one million bpd, in its monthly Oil Market Report.
"North American demand has been revised upwards by 270,000 bpd from last month's report to 20.6 million bpd. This is an annual increase of 3.6 percent or 700,000 bpd," the IEA said.
U.S. demand is expected to have grown by 4.0 percent or 720,000 bpd in June, with strong demand growth for all products except gasoline, which increased by only 0.5 percent.
By contrast, estimates of European demand in the second quarter was revised downwards by 100,000 bpd to 13.8 million bpd, an annual increase of 2.4 percent or 300,000 bpd.

Consumption in the four largest countries in May fell by 290,000 bpd due to fewer working days, a build in German heating oil stocks the previous month and inter-fuel competition which affected fuel oil deliveries in Britain, the Paris-based agency said.
OECD demand in 1998 is projected to increase by one percent, or 400,000 bpd to 42.1 million bpd, a slightly slower rate of growth than this year.
Accelerating economic growth in Japan and Europe will be more than offset by an anticipated slowdown in the U.S. economy, the IEA said.
